sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) Ocean Box Brokerage

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong commercial codification; Private Interest Foundation modelled on Liechtenstein foundation law principles)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force 31 October 2012 (Chapter 10 Investment; Annex 10-B expropriation)
Panama–Republic of Korea Free Trade Agreement, in force 1 March 2021
Panama–Taiwan Free Trade Agreement, in force 1 January 2004
European Union–Central America Association Agreement (provisional application for Panama from 2013)
Panama–Singapore Double Taxation Agreement (in force 1990, as amended)

Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID), Panama party since 1996

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework for financial and non-financial designated subjects, amended by Law 70 of 2019); Executive Decree 363 of 2015 (implementing regulations); Law 70 of 30 October 2019 (mandatory Ultimate Beneficial Owner register at the Registro Público de Panamá); Resolution SSNF 480 of 2019 (UBO due diligence protocol); Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations and Executive Decree 24 of 1996; Law 38 of 2000 (Administrative Procedure Law); Law 41 of 2007 (financing of terrorism offences and UAF powers)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or civil registry authority of the founder's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Certificate of Good Standing of the founder (if the founder is a corporate legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chamber of Commerce / Company Registry of the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds sworn declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder's banking institution and the founder/settlor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization with notary attestation plus Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn statement of beneficial ownership and PEP status of founder, council members, and designated protector
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each relevant natural person before a notary public of their residence jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement of any corporate founder and its group structure chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization at a Panamanian consulate or Hague Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening of the founder, foundation council members, protector, known beneficiaries, and any service providers against the OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the consolidated sanctions/terrorist list published by the Panamanian Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); enhanced customer due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 and Resolution SSNF 480 requires written risk rating, adverse-media screening, PEP database cross-checks, and independent verification of source of funds; residency agents must retain screening evidence for a minimum of five years and report suspicious activity to the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica of the Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama online platform) — Nominal Certificate / Certificado de No Objeción issuance service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation name may be expressed in Spanish or any foreign language; however, the statutory suffix 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' is mandatory in the foundation's corporate name; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters and filed in a Spanish-translated form; the underlying constitutive deed must be written in Spanish before a Panamanian notary, with sworn translation if the foreign-language name is used.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: TRUST (Financial and trust company licence required)
VALORES / SECURITIES (Securities market regulator approval required)
FONDO DE PENSIONES / PENSION FUND (Pension supervisor licence required)
ESTADO / GOBIERNO / MINISTERIO / NACIONAL / OFICIAL (Terms implying Panamanian government affiliation require prior ministerial approval)
MUNICIPIO / POLICÍA / ADUANAS / CANAL DE PANAMÁ (Protected public or institutional designations)
UNIVERSIDAD / COLEGIO / HOSPITAL (Regulated professions and institutions requiring specific ministry approval)
FUNDACIÓN (Sensitive reserved token when implying public-interest status; private interest foundations must use 'Fundación de Interés Privado' precisely)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the nominal certificate is rejected, the applicant has ten (10) business days to file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Directora General del Registro Público de Panamá; upon denial or silence of the Reconsideración, a 'Recurso de Apelación' may be filed with the Junta Directiva del Registro Público within five (5) business days of notification, in accordance with Law 38 of 2000; alternatively, the applicant may withdraw and resubmit a new name application at a cost of a fresh nominal certificate fee. Rejection grounds follow the non-confusion, non-idoneity, and statutory suffix requirements of the Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado and registry practice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Private Interest Foundation must maintain a registered office in Panama at the physical office address of its licensed resident agent (abogado idóneo), where service of process and statutory notices are received; pure virtual mail-forwarding addresses are not recognised as registered offices. The foundation's operational management of NVOCC cargo services may be conducted from abroad through its commercial arm or third-party subcontractors, but the Panamanian registered office must remain a genuine, staffed location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium (estimated 30–40% cumulative probability over the first three (3) years of operation): the NVOCC/freight-forwarding business class is classified as a 'non-financial designated subject' under Law 23 of 2015, and the Registro Público and the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF) retain authority to conduct unannounced inspections of the registered office and UBO records, particularly where wire transfer and ACH payment volumes exceed USD 1,000,000 per annum.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial corporate books, share/foundation records register, common seal, and accounting chart set-up
NVOCC regulatory pre-incorporation advisory for ISIC 5229 ocean freight forwarding (licence structuring, customs guarantee assessment and FMC-equivalent Panama maritime authority review)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Ley No. 41 de 2013, Arts. 1-40
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter) and Reglamento (Foundation Purpose Rules)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama PIF legislation does not require a statutory minimum paid-up capital or a bank escrow. The Foundation Charter must declare an initial endowment, customarily USD 10,000, and the founder must contribute that endowment according to the payment terms stated in the charter. A notarized declaration of receipt suffices for registry; no escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [PA_PIF FOUNDATION] On this [day] of [month], 2025, the Founder, having subscribed the initial endowment of US$10,000 in accordance with the Foundation Charter, resolves: (1) to adopt the registered office at City of Panama, Republic of Panama, and to entrust its maintenance to a qualified resident agent; (2) to approve the appointment of the first Foundation Council composed of [Name], [Name] and [Name], with full powers to administer foundation assets; (3) to appoint [Name] as Protector with supervisory rights; and (4) to authorize the Council to open bank accounts, execute the NVOCC license application, and issue operational instructions. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Foundation Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Foundation Section, online 'Vista Nominal' module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-clearance request electronically or in person at the Foundation Section of the Public Registry. The examiner verifies that the proposed foundation name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporation, foundation, or registered commercial name. Upon approval, obtain the name-clearance certificate with the applicable validity period.
required_dossiers: Application signed by the founder for 'Vista Nominal y Documental'
Certificate of no objection from other registry sections, if required
Copy of founder's passport or, if founder is a legal entity, corporate resolution and current registration documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is objected, file a new clearance request with a different name or add a distinctive suffix such as the year or jurisdiction indicator, and pay the applicable re-issuance fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian notary to draft the Acta Constitutiva in Spanish, including clauses for the foundation name, registered office, resident agent, foundation council, protector, initial endowment, beneficiaries, and the lawful purpose of ocean freight forwarding and NVOCC operations. If used, the Reglamento must be drafted and executed contemporaneously with the Charter.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter
Draft Reglamento, if any
Identity documents of the founder and intended foundation council members
Brief written statement of lawful purpose referencing ISIC 5229 and NVOCC activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests revised wording, amend the draft to eliminate any corporate or share-based references and align all clauses with Law No. 25 of 1995 before re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder must appear physically or through a power of attorney before the notary, sign each page of the Charter and Regulation, and declare that the initial endowment has been subscribed. The notary records the instrument in the protocol register and issues certified copies.
required_dossiers: Signed Foundation Charter and Regulation
Power of attorney if the founder is represented
Valid passport or national identity document of signatories
Receipt for notarial protocol and transcription fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution on legal formatting grounds, file a corrective addendum clarifying the registered office city, endowment payment terms, or foundation purpose, and then re-execute the instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter and Regulation, together with the name-clearance certificate and proof of payment of registry fees. The Registry will examine the documents for formal compliance, assign a file number, and if no observations are issued, record the foundation and provide its Certificate of Registration and legal personality (Personería Jurídica).
required_dossiers: Certified protocol copy or original notarial extract of the Foundation Charter
Name-clearance certificate
Proof of payment of the official filing fee
Completed registry cover sheet or form for foundation inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a notice of observations, submit a responsive brief or an amended charter within five business days addressing each objection, then re-present the document for inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification and Corporate Books Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Impuestos (DGI) and Registro Público de Panamá - Books Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Personería Jurídica, obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) from the Panamanian tax authority, registering the economic activity code for ISIC 5229 and NVOCC services. Register the minute book, ledger, and share or foundation council records section at the Public Registry, and maintain the resident agent contract at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Foundation Registration and legal personality
RUC application form duly completed by a legal representative
Certified copy of the first Foundation Council resolution
Lease agreement or proof of physical registered office
Resident agent services contract and notarized acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects or suspends the RUC application due to an incorrect economic activity code, file a rectification request and attach the NVOCC license application to demonstrate the lawful scope of operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP) - Dirección de Servicios Marítimos Auxiliares
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Operador de Carga Marítima - NVOCC (Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección Nacional de Evaluación y Seguimiento Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I - Environmental Registration (ficha de registro) for standard administrative freight-forwarding offices; full EIA Report becomes mandatory only if the operation includes cargo warehousing, cold storage, or pier-side handling exceeding Category II thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For office-only NVOCC operations there is zero process wastewater; sanitary effluent must comply with Panamanian discharge norms of pH 6-9, total suspended solids not exceeding 100 mg/L, and oil and grease not exceeding 30 mg/L. Incidental container or cargo maintenance, if undertaken, must not emit volatile organic compounds in localized concentrations above 20 ppm, and any packaging wastes must be handled through MiAMBIENTE-authorized waste operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural load inspection certificate for any cargo-storage or container-stuffing area issued by the municipal engineering window; and workplace health and safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), including the mandatory safety and hygiene committee when staffing exceeds ten employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), the unitary national revenue directorate. Registration, e-filing and electronic clearance are performed via the DGI's Sede Electrónica portal (https://sedeelectronica.dgi.gob.pa; information portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa). Ancillary authorities relevant to NVOCC exporters: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) for export declarations and customs export validation, and the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá for FX remittance certificates and bank confirmations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional) before a notary and register the Private Interest Foundation at the Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público); the charter must state a minimum patrimony of B/. 10,000 (Law 25 of 1995, as amended) and appoint a Resident Agent (Agente Residente). Step 2: Pay the mandatory annual registry fee (Tasa Única de B/. 300) to the Treasury via the Registro Público to maintain juridical good standing. Step 3: Obtain the Panamanian Digital Signature (Firma Digital) from an ANCE-certified certification authority (e.g., T-Sign, Apoyo Legal) to access Sede Electrónica. Step 4: File the RUC application (Formulario Único de Inscripción) electronically via Sede Electrónica, attaching: (a) certified copy of the Foundation Certificate issued by the Registro Público; (b) resident agent acceptance and notarized power of attorney; (c) passport copies of the Foundation Council members and the beneficial owner declaration; (d) Aviso de Operación/Licencia Comercial issued by the municipal or commerce authorities if business is conducted in Panama; (e) identification of the legal representative. Step 5: DGI assigns the RUC number (legal-entity format, e.g., '1-155-XXXXXX-XXXXX') within 5–10 business days; the same registration creates the ITBMS taxpayer account. Step 6: For NVOCC operations, obtain the AMP freight forwarding/NVOCC license from the Autoridad Marítima de Panamá and the customs brokerage authorization from ANA. Step 7: Register accounting books with DGI and retain a licensed Panamanian CPA for certification of Panama-source income and annual financial statements if required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — the PIF is a distinct juridical person taxed only on Panama-source income (Fiscal Code Arts. 694–696). Foreign-source freight, chartering, brokerage and financial income are outside the Panamanian income tax base. NVOCC income from port-to-port ocean carriage originating in Panama and services used or exploited within Panama is treated as Panama-source; pure offshore brokerage between foreign shippers and consignees remains untaxed. Entity_Level_Taxation applies on Panama-source net profits at the 25% corporate ISR rate; no pass-through treatment exists. An inactive PIF with no Panama-source income is not required to file income tax returns but remains subject to the annual B/. 300 registry fee.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or standalone hybrid mismatch elections exist in Panamanian law; tax classification is statutory under the territoriality principle. Available elections and regimes: (1) Inactive/Passive Foundation election: certify no Panama-source business activity and remain dormant for ISR/ITBMS purposes; (2) Charitable-exempt election: apply to MEF for income tax exemption under Fiscal Code Art. 679 if the foundation is dedicated exclusively to charitable, educational, scientific or cultural purposes, and remove the NVOCC business scope from the charter; (3) Branch/PE profit-allocation election: operate the NVOCC activity through a registered Panamanian branch of the PIF and allocate profit under transfer pricing rules (Law 52 of 2016); (4) Dividend/profit-distribution election: capitalise vs. distribute Panama-source profits under the 10%–15% dividend withholding regime; (5) Deemed-export election: if located in a Colon Free Zone or authorised logistics park, elect ITBMS deemed-export treatment for qualifying re-invoicing transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's VAT-equivalent transfer tax), regulated by Fiscal Code Arts. 1057-A to 1057-V, Executive Decree 84 of 2006, and DGI implementing resolutions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de-minimis exemption: any entity performing taxable transfers of goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must obtain RUC/ITBMS registration. Small-taxpayer simplification: annual gross income up to B/. 36,000 qualifies for the simplified 'pequeño contribuyente' quota regime (Executive Decree 84 of 2006, as amended). Mandatory e-invoicing threshold: annual gross income above B/. 250,000 obligates full electronic issuance (DGI Resolution 202-13894 of 2020, as amended). DGI may designate a taxpayer as Gran Contribuyente based on turnover or fiscal relevance, imposing monthly filing and specialized payment obligations. An NVOCC invoicing outbound ocean freight is structurally engaged in taxable activities; recommended practice is to register for ITBMS from the date the RUC is granted regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory. Panama's Facturación Electrónica de Panamá regime requires all Grandes Contribuyentes to issue XML/XAdES invoices through DGI Sede Electrónica or certified API and obtain the DGI 'Código de Autorización' before issuance (real-time pre-clearance). The authorisation QR code must appear on the issued invoice. Under phased DGI Resolution 202-13894 of 2020 and Resolution 201-10241 of 2023, taxpayers with annual turnover above B/. 250,000 migrated to full e-invoicing during 2023–2024; all ITBMS taxpayers, including small registrants, must adopt by the 2025 deadline. Monthly ITBMS declarations (Form 430) are filed through the same platform; export zero-rated invoices must be flagged with the export tariff code. Non-compliant issuers face per-invoice fines of approximately B/. 50–B/. 500, denial of input VAT credit claims, and elevated fiscal risk ratings.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) applies to: (i) physical exports of goods accompanied by an ANA export declaration; (ii) services 'used or exploited abroad' under Fiscal Code Art. 1057-V and DGI guidelines, covering international maritime freight, ocean freight forwarding and NVOCC services rendered to non-resident principals for cargo moving between Panamanian ports and foreign ports or entirely between foreign points; (iii) services to vessels operating in international traffic, including container handling invoiced as part of the international freight contract; (iv) deemed exports for services provided to Colon Free Zone operators with prior ANA authorisation. To qualify, the NVOCC must: (a) bill freight and forwarding charges in foreign currency to a non-resident counterparty; (b) evidence physical movement of containers out of Panama through an ocean Bill of Lading showing a Panamanian load port and foreign discharge port; (c) demonstrate that the beneficial use of the service occurs abroad, e.g., destination charges, foreign agency fees, or port-to-port ocean carriage. Services considered domestic and standard-rated at 7% include local drayage between the Panamanian port and the importer's warehouse, separately invoiced terminal handling, warehousing within Panama, and inbound freight collection services rendered to Panamanian importers. Mixed contracts must state an explicit cost-allocation schedule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduana – Exportación) issued by Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), showing port of loading in Panama and port of discharge abroad for goods covered by the freight contract

Bill of Lading – Ocean or Master B/L (NVOCC House B/L plus underlying Carrier Master B/L when the PIF issues the HBL) evidencing cargo movement and freight payable by a non-resident shipper, consignee, or the foreign NVOCC principal

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa Bancaria) issued by a Panamanian licensed bank evidencing collection of export proceeds within the statutory period; Swift Wire or ACH confirmation must name the NVOCC as beneficiary and the foreign client as remitter
Commercial invoice and executed ocean freight forwarding / slot charter contract between the PIF and the non-resident principal, including Incoterms, freight split, and commission structure
ITBMS refund application and supporting schedules (Solicitud de Devolución de Créditos Fiscales) filed via Sede Electrónica when input VAT credits are claimed on export costs
Proof of valid AMP NVOCC license and ANA customs brokerage authorization for the operating entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI's fiscalization directorate, jointly with ANA, audits zero-rated exporters on a documentary and bank-ledger basis. Refund denial triggers include: (i) absence of FX remittance within 180 days from the bill-of-lading date; (ii) cancelled or no-show customs export declarations; (iii) invoices issued to related offshore entities without economic substance, resulting in GAAR or transfer-pricing recharacterization under Law 52 of 2016; (iv) evidence that cargo never left Panamanian waters. If zero-rating is rejected, DGI reissues the transaction as domestic 7% ITBMS and levies retroactive interest at 1.5% per month (approximately 18% annualized), late-payment surcharges, and fines of 50% to 200% of the omitted tax (Fiscal Code Art. 760). Deliberate fraud triggers criminal tax evasion prosecution, punishable by 2 to 5 years of imprisonment under the Panamanian Criminal Code as amended by Law 38 of 2013, administrative cancellation of the RUC, the AMP NVOCC licence, and AEO status, plus disqualification of resident agents. Taxpayers may appeal through the Recurso de Apelación before the DGI and the Tribunal Administrativo Tributario, but must first pay 50% of the assessed amount or post a bond.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), created by Decree Law No. 2 of 2008, supervises licensed banks and acts as the de facto foreign-exchange and payments regulator; the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) manages sovereign finance. The US Dollar is legal tender per the Currency Law of 1904 (as codified), so monetary policy is effectively set by the US Federal Reserve and all bank clearing is USD-denominated; the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) performs AML/CFT surveillance under Law 23 of 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current- and capital-account convertibility with zero exchange controls. Because Panama is fully dollarized, there are no capital-repatriation approvals, no profit-remittance hurdles, no currency fragmentation, and no restrictions on non-resident ownership or repatriation of foundation assets. Panama's territorial tax regime taxes only Panama-source income; non-resident founders and beneficiaries may freely receive PIF dividends or liquidation proceeds, although distributions from Panama-source profits attract a 10% dividend withholding tax under the general regime (reduced rates apply under special regimes). CRS/FATCA reporting does not restrict convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion, repatriation timeline, or foreign-currency retention ratio for NVOCC freight receipts or any other export/transport earnings. Foreign-currency proceeds may be retained or converted at freely quoted commercial bank rates; the only applicable constraints are AML record-keeping and retention of underlying transport documents for five years under Law 23 of 2015.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (PIF endowment) + Operational USD Corporate Checking with SWIFT global rail
Capital Escrow Account + Operational USD Corporate Checking with dedicated foundation and trust desks
Operational USD Corporate Checking + Trade Finance (LC/Standby) + Foreign Exchange lines
Operational USD Corporate Checking + ACH Direct deposit accounts
Operational USD Corporate Checking + Escrow/Custody accounts
Operational USD Corporate Checking + Regional ACH Direct clearing for Central America
Operational USD Corporate Checking only (retail savings bank profile)
Operational USD Corporate Checking (public-sector and government deposit focus)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium as a primary treasury rail; Medium only as a complementary collection switch. Panama's Law No. 71 of 2019 Fintech Hub (SBP sandbox) does not create a general electronic-money-institution (EMI) license; non-resident offshore EMIs cannot obtain a Panama master account without an SBP-licensed correspondent, and almost all global EMIs classify NVOCC/freight forwarding as high-risk under their acceptable-use policies due to trade-based money-laundering exposure. The PIF legal form adds further friction because foundations are registered in the Public Registry rather than the Mercantile Registry, which many foreign EMIs do not recognize. Recommended architecture: principal USD clearing at a Tier-1 SBP bank plus a niche shipping-focused remittance fintech limited to low-value agent payouts; never route high-value freight settlement through an unregulated EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: SBP Agreement No. 1 of 2015 and Law 23 of 2015 require in-person identification of the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one Foundation Council signatory for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced entity. In practice, Banco General, Banistmo and Multibank require a physical interview at account opening; Towerbank and Global Bank accept a remote video interview when a licensed Panama attorney / registered agent provides an introducer certification and all documents are apostilled (foundation public-registry record, council resolution, passports, source of funds). The recommended protocol is a one-time physical visit by the PIF's designated council member with a Panama-licensed counsel's cover letter, which removes the uncertainty of remote enhanced due diligence for a NVOCC operator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee Foundation Council and unidentified beneficiaries (PIF opacity).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full foundation public-registry record (inscripción), Acta Constitutiva and Reglamento, current Foundation Council resolution opening the bank account, identity and source-of-wealth declarations for the founder and all named beneficiaries, UAF (FIU) background-clearance confirmation, and a legal opinion confirming the foundation's intended lawful purpose under Law 25 of 1995.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed freight brokering — NVOCC activity without Panama Maritime Authority (AMP) registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified AMP NVOCC registration or pending application with the Junta Técnica de Agentes Navieros, specimen House Bill of Lading (HBL) and Master Bill of Lading (MBL), published freight tariff, master service contracts with vessel-operating carriers, cargo liability / errors-and-omissions insurance certificate, and an operational substance file (office lease, payroll, logistics accounting system).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering indicators: over/under-invoicing, split payments, or unexplained freight-rate deviations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-shipment booking file: client freight invoice, packing list, HBL/MBL numbers, container numbers, ACP vessel-rotation call, third-party carrier rate sheet, and a 12-month receivables/payables aging demonstrating consistent commission margins between 3% and 10%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure: cargo or counterparties touching OFAC, EU, or UN restricted parties (Cuba, Venezuela, Iran, Syria, North Korea, Russia).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written Sanctions Compliance Program, five-year restricted-party screening log (SDN, EU consolidated sanctions, UN listings) covering all shippers, consignees, vessels, and ports of call, negative-news monitoring reports, and contractual embargo clauses incorporated into every booking contract; the Panama bank operates within the OFAC-responsive USD clearing system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax transparency mismatches: CRS/FATCA classification confusion for the hybrid PIF vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS self-certification (Form W-8IMY or equivalent) for the foundation and its beneficiaries, FATCA GIIN registration or affirmative non-FI legal analysis, a territoriality tax memo from a Panamanian certified public accountant confirming non-BEPS exposure, and proof of DGI corporate tax filings for the NVOCC operating account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the PIF's initial endowment (minimum USD 10,000 under Law 25 of 1995) and later working-capital injections is a SWIFT MT103 (with a separate MT202 cover for high-value transfers) from the founder's or investing entity's account to the PIF's Capital Escrow / Operational Account at the selected Panama bank. Field 70 should state: 'PIF ENDOWMENT CAPITAL - LAW 25 DE 1995 - PA_PIF - founder reference'; working-capital loans must reference 'NVOCC WORKING CAPITAL LOAN' and be supported by a signed promissory note. Verification documents: apostilled founding charter, council resolution opening the account, source-of-funds declaration, and originator bank reference; no exchange approval or tax-clearance certificate is required because Panama has no capital controls. Freight receivables arrive by wire or ACH Direct and are automatically reconciled to the HBL/invoice number under Law 23 of 2015 record-retention rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for carrier, port, bunker, and agent payments; SBP-licensed banks clear USD through US correspondents (JPMorgan, Citibank), and field 70 must carry the HBL/MBL and commercial invoice reference for pre-payment sanctions screening. High-value staged payments (charter hire, stevedoring contracts) are settled by Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700 issued by the Panama bank, confirmed at the beneficiary's bank). Domestic port fees, ACP canal transits, payroll, and low-value supplier payments use ACH Direct and intra-bank sweeps, with a next-day sweep between the Operational and Capital Escrow Accounts to preserve the PIF's capital encumbrance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC FX Forward (Deliverable) — tenor-matched USD/EUR, USD/CNY, and USD/COP hedging executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with an SBP-licensed counterparty
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) — for emerging-market currencies with offshore restrictions (BRL, COP, ARS) under which only USD differentials are settled at maturity

Cross-Currency Swap / Short-dated FX Swap — conversion of the freight dollar float into EUR/CNY for scheduled Asian and Mediterranean agent disbursements, plus rollover swaps for intra-month liquidity smoothing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax payment and declaration (Tasa Única Anual for Private Interest Foundations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, with payment processed on behalf of the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 June of each calendar year; newly formed PIFs are administratively integrated into the payment cycle in the second calendar year after registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a USD 100 surcharge from 1 July and an additional USD 100 after 31 December; three consecutive unpaid years give the Registro Público authority to administratively strike off the foundation and cancel the registered agent appointment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual NVOCC licence renewal, including financial responsibility bond or insurance certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP), Dirección de Operaciones Marítimas y Comercio Civil
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal on the licence anniversary; application and payment must be submitted no later than 30 days before the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accrual of a monthly late fee of USD 100; non-renewal for 90 days results in suspension of the NVOCC billing authority, cancellation of the AMP operational permit, and the requirement to file a new application with fresh bond evidence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is required when annual gross revenue of the Panama entity exceeds USD 1,000,000, total assets exceed USD 3,000,000, or the NVOCC operating subsidiary is required by AMP or its securities/fidelity bond issuer to present audited financial statements; otherwise, a dormant PIF with no Panama-source income may file the annual franchise tax without audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; Panama SMEs may apply the IFRS for SMEs Standard, provided the PIF does not hold public fundraising securities and does not conduct regulated banking or insurance activities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must ratify the list of beneficiaries and ultimate beneficial owners by a private act signed within the first 90 days of each calendar year; the resident agent must receive a sworn UBO confirmation for retention in the foundation's confidential file, and any transfer of beneficial interest or foundation rights must be recorded in the Private Registry and reflected in the council minutes within 30 days of the effective transfer. No public filing of beneficial owners is made, but the complete registry must be available for lawful inspection by the Panama Tax Authority on request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (private interests and founder rights ledger)
Minute Book (Actas de Sesiones del Consejo), Secretary Book, and Confidential Beneficiary Register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 to USD 4,500 per annum when audited financial statements are prepared

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source exclusivity: only Panama-source earnings are subject to the 25% corporate rate; foreign-source income derived by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in NVOCC ocean freight mediation is statutorily exempt, creating an effective 0% Panama tax burden on international brokerage profits. PIFs may also apply the tax-neutrality doctrine of Law 25 of 1995, and non-taxable foundations pay only a flat annual government fee of B/. 300. A Multinational Headquarters (SEM) licence, if separately held, reduces the residual dividend rate and exempts logistics-related foreign-source revenues.
